why_now: Weapons-component drawings are almost certainly controlled unclassified information (CUI). CMMC Phase 2 is paused, but DFARS 7012, NIST SP 800-171 and an SPRS score are required today, and a 25-person shop rarely has someone who owns that.
angle: NIST 800-171 gap assessment, SPRS score, and a managed environment for CUI, so they're ready when CMMC certification restarts.
subject: Your SPRS score while CMMC is paused
body:
Hi {first_name},

With CMMC Phase 2 paused since July, a lot of DoD shops have put compliance on the back burner. The catch is that DFARS 7012 and NIST 800-171 still apply to any contract with controlled drawings, and primes are still asking suppliers for their SPRS scores.

For a shop making small-arms components, that's likely you. infinIT is a Northeast Ohio IT and security firm (35+ years, in-house team) that helps manufacturers close 800-171 gaps without disrupting production, so certification is a formality when it restarts.

Would a 20-minute call to talk through where you stand be worth it?

[Rep name]
infinIT
fu1: Hi {first_name}, following up. If it's useful, we can start with a short gap review against the 110 NIST 800-171 controls and help you confirm your SPRS score is accurate. An inflated score is the bigger risk under the False Claims Act.
fu2: Hi {first_name}, last note. When CMMC restarts, assessor calendars will fill fast. If you want to get ahead of it, I'm at [phone].
notes: Don't assume what's on their SPRS record; ask.
